title: Ambulatory Step-up Dosing of Elranatamab: An Observational Feasibility and Safety Evaluation of an Outpatient Approach Using Remote Monitoring and Emergency Therapy Plans
summary: The initial doses of the drug elranatamab may cause serious side effects such as fever, chills, circulatory problems, or nausea, which can have serious consequences if left untreated. For this reason, the first doses (initial dosing) are typically administered and monitored in an inpatient  setting. However, with appropriately structured monitoring and emergency treatment plans, outpatient administration of the first doses of elranatamab is also possible. The goal of the SAFESTEP study is to investigate the feasibility and safety of this outpatient step up dosing of elranatamab using remote monitoring and emergency treatment plans.
conditions: Multiple myeloma Without mention of complete remission

interventions.name: This is a non-interventional observational study. As part of the study, patients will complete quality-of-life questionnaires and, optionally, provide 1 stool sample and 1–3 blood samples. Data collection will take place over 56 days, including 28 days of continuous data collection during the first

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Choice of outpatient Elranatamab step-up dosing program
Exclusion criteria:
concurrent participation in an interventional clinical trial
